# Charter — T3 PM job (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** T3 'PM job', track v2, ADM phase G, tranche 3, project `01a1d039-0d33-7915-8833-75f4dc31cc07`, plan `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12`. The record carries `meta.measured_status: built`, `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`, `meta.closure_outputs: [closure-review]`, closed issue #74 and a reopen dated 2026-11-26T07:44:41Z. The scope baseline `01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa` was taken on 2026-11-26 and approved by `01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545`; the rework runs under delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** deliver the PM job of SPEC_V2 §12 — charter, WBS, baseline, staffing, gate routing and closure — so that a PM runs a request end to end, cannot approve its own gate, and a baseline change requires a change request. The tranche-3 review recorded T3 as closed without its live delivery contract and its Phase-G review; the project was reopened on 2026-11-26 to complete the record, not to add scope. This retrospective reconstitutes the MSP/TOGAF lifecycle record for the PM job: charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, the project-brief and evidence outputs and the closure review.
- **Scope:** the governance of a single project request from charter to closure — the chartered scope, the WBS and its four WSJF inputs 8, 8, 5, 3, the scope baseline and its change control, the staffing plan, the gate router that keeps the approver distinct from the requester, the closure record and its declared outputs. Out of scope is the decision ladder's policy engine (T2), the kanban coach (T4), the kata (T5), the tool platform (T13) and a re-implementation of the T1 plan spine; the rework adds no feature and re-opens no V1 slice.
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26; it records the lifecycle of the PM job recorded as built under issue #74 and reviewed by the tranche-3 review `01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9`, it does not authorise new work.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T3 PM job (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

body.assignment: Rework T3 by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable and the Phase-G review, and re-publish the project-brief and evidence outputs. The architecture work is the PM job itself — one project run from charter through WBS, scope baseline, staffing, gate routing and closure, with the approver kept distinct from the requester and every baseline change carried by a change request — recorded retrospectively and dated 2026-11-26.
body.scope: In scope: the charter and its approved gate; the WBS with the four typed WSJF inputs 8, 8, 5, 3; the scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa taken on 2026-11-26 and approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545; the staffing plan; the gate router that refuses self-approval and records every decision; the change request that must precede a baseline change; the closure record with its closure-review output; the seven A–D artefacts and the project registers. Out of scope: the T2 decision ladder's policy engine, the T4 coach, the T5 kata, the T13 tool platform, the T1 plan spine's implementation and every V1 slice; the rework completes the record and adds no scope.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the #526 rework delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14; the Architecture Board reviews the seven A–D artefacts, which this pack records as approved. The programme owner is the approver of the delivery contract and of the closure: the scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa is approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545, and the closure gate recorded for T3 was decided by an approver distinct from its requester, which is the gate's own rule. The PM runs the request and may not approve a gate it raised.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate in SPEC_V2 §12 is executable: a PM runs a request end to end; the PM cannot approve its own gate; a baseline change requires a change request. The close gate reads the project's declared outputs — project-brief and evidence — plus the closure-review output, a live board-approved delivery contract, a Phase-G review citing the standing delegation, the approved scope baseline, the seven mandatory A–D artefacts with their registers, WBS inputs 8, 8, 5, 3, a demo credit per accepted deliverable and at least one tranche lesson. This content pack is checked offline by scripts/rework-content-check.py --project T3 before the factory reads it, and the factory then records the contract, review, artefacts and closure against the snapshot.
body.contract: This statement is authored retrospectively under the delegation and is approved through the same board gate it describes; its approval is recorded by the factory from this pack, not asserted here. It is complemented by the delivery contract whose commitments, compliance and approval fields this pack authors, on the approved scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa (kind scope, taken 2026-11-26, approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545), and by the Phase-G review the factory records from this pack. The tranche-3 review 01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9 decided continue on 2026-11-26 and authorised tranche 4; the reopen this pack answers is dated 2026-11-26T07:44:41Z and its reason is the missing contract, review and baseline record.

# Architecture Artefact Index — T3 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Metadata

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: Stakeholder map — PM job (matrix), Driver/goal/objective — PM job (catalog), Requirements catalog — PM job (catalog), Solution concept — PM job (diagram), Business capability map — PM job (diagram), Data entity catalog — PM job (catalog) and Technology standards — PM job (catalog). ## Outcome

T3 delivered the PM job of SPEC_V2 §12: a PM runs a project request end to end through charter, WBS, baseline, staffing, gate routing and closure; the PM cannot approve a gate it raised; and a baseline change requires a change request. Out of scope: the T2 decision ladder's policy engine, which the PM job reads rather than re-implements; the T4 kanban coach, the T5 kata and the T13 tool platform; the T1 plan spine's implementation, which T1 owns; and every V1 slice, which the V2 plan does not re-open. The PM job reuses the plan spine T1 establishes — wbs_node, project_baseline, project_register_item and project_dependency — and the decision records T2 produces rather than inventing a second approval store. The project is its own inception unit: the plan is docs/SPEC_V2.md#12, the T3 row is the analysis the work starts from, and issue #74 is the claim that closed with the build. The tranche-3 review 01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9 decided continue on 2026-11-26, and the project was reopened the same day because the record lacked its live contract, its Phase-G review and its baseline. Downstream, T4 depends on T3, T9 and T10 depend on T1 and T3, and T18 depends on T0, T1, T2 and T3, so a change to the PM job's gate vocabulary or closure outputs is felt by every consumer. In governance the project depends on the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14 and on the approved scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa.

The PM job exercises seven capabilities: chartered execution, sized decomposition with four WSJF inputs, a frozen scope baseline, staffed delivery with a named owner per deliverable, independent gate routing that keeps the approver distinct from the requester, controlled change through a change request, and complete closure on a live contract, a Phase-G review and the declared outputs. The build closed issue #74 with measured_status built; the tranche-3 review on 2026-11-26 reopened the project because the governance record lacked its contract, review and baseline; the 2026-11-26 retrospective rework authors this pack, and the factory writes the artefacts, registers, contract, review, baseline acceptance and closure from it. # Closure review — T3 PM job (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is the PM job of SPEC_V2 §12: a PM runs a request end to end, cannot approve its own gate, and a baseline change requires a change request. The record supports it: the build is recorded as measured_status built under closed issue #74, the scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa is approved by 01a1e8a7-8b23-76a9-9114-aafb95f7a545, the closure gate was decided by an approver distinct from its requester, the charter gate is approved, and the declared outputs project-brief, evidence and closure-review are published. Against that, the pre-rework receipt docs/evidence/rework/T3.json was red on contract, review, artefact standard and rework resolution; this pack supplies the rows those checks read, so the acceptance is met on the completed record rather than on the earlier red one.

## Evidence
The evidence is the snapshot record: the project 01a1d039-0d33-7915-8833-75f4dc31cc07, the approved scope baseline 01a216d0-9c9b-7c8c-a6ef-0d9365632efa with its approver, closed issue #74, the tranche-3 review 01a216d0-d634-738e-985a-00a85cfd48d9 and the published outputs of 2026-11-26 — evidence 01a1ee73-db2e-76b5-8c92-076f14dc94ec, project brief 01a216d0-68e5-764d-92af-9864ddae5127, closure review 01a216d0-6635-720e-84e9-005ba604d06f and architecture artefact index 01a216d0-69ec-7512-85db-3a22b7b00241. The seven A–D artefacts, the five register kinds, the delivery contract and the WBS deliverable are the records this pack authors and the factory writes; the rework receipt remains the statement of what was missing before them.

## Open items

Two items remain visible. First, the record is reconstructed from the snapshot facts, the SPEC_V2 row and the existing receipt; it does not replay each PM run that preceded the rework, so it evidences the lifecycle and its gate decisions rather than every execution step. Second, the pre-rework receipt named seed_live_drift:T3 among its unresolved P0/P1 packages; the factory's live publish of this record clears it, and this review does not claim that publish has already happened. Neither item is a scope gap, and neither is waived: both are stated as limits of the retrospective record.

The retrospective decision is to close T3 on the record the rework completes, at the level compliant that the Phase-G review records against the delivery contract this pack authors, with the pre-rework red receipt and the seed-live drift named rather than hidden. The decision is dated 2026-11-26 and rests on the approved baseline, the distinct closure approver, closed issue #74 and the published outputs; it does not add scope, does not reclassify any earlier row, and does not assert a re-measurement of the PM job's original runs. The project closes with the record it now carries, and the durable correction is that a closure without a contract, a Phase-G review and its declared outputs is refused before it can read green.
